title: The Craftmasons and the road to the Council
summary: Why the Traditions first came together.

claims.text: By the 14th century mage affairs across Europe and Asia were in chaos, and the idea of a Council of Nine grew from that confusion.
At the heart of the Order of Reason stood the Craftmasons, engineers and reformers who wanted order in Europe and an end to the monsters preying on people.
The egalitarian Craftmasons came to loathe the elitist Order of Hermes and gathered allies against it.

title: Mistridge, the dragons and Horizon
summary: The battle that won the Hermetics their sway over the Council.

claims.text: When the Order of Reason struck, the Hermetics called up more than a dozen dragons bound by pact, and the beasts mauled the artificers' army.
That rescue explains the Order of Hermes' outsize say in Council policy and why the others tolerate it.
The mystics then built Horizon, a realm in the spirit world fed by Nodes worldwide, where the Council and the Nine Traditions were formalised.

title: The Balamob
summary: Mayan jaguar priests brought to the new Convocation.

claims.text: The Balamob hold blood and other bodily fluids sacred as the sap of the world tree, and bloodletting lets the priest reach Xibalba.
Each initiate meets a wayob, a companion spirit that guides and guards and, for the Awakened, is the Avatar.
Known for jaguar shapeshifting, divination and astrology, most live among the Maya of southern Mexico and Guatemala and often clash with local armies.
Masters are the teachers and leaders of mage society, often holding power in a Chantry or Tradition; most Council Heralds, Justices and Executioners are Masters.
Archmage is the highest rank and is now very rare.
Whether Oracles are Ascended Archmages is still argued.
A Chantry may be a coven, a lodge, a software studio, an assassins' guild or a rock band; being solitary carries no shame, but groups bring real advantages.
A cult of followers adds successes to rituals when all of it gathers, from three for 13-17 members up to five for 23-27.

title: Sanctum
summary: A personal space shaped to a mage's paradigm.

claims.text: A Sanctum forms slowly, at least five years of work per dot, and suits only its owner's paradigm, an apprentice's or one directly shared.
Its protection covers only effects cast inside; an effect reaching out, such as by Correspondence, takes full Paradox and likely unravels.
A mage could stay unaging inside a Sanctum yet age quickly after leaving.

title: The Staff of Heralds
summary: A Wonder made to prove a messenger's standing.

claims.text: A few great Wonders belong to all the Traditions and matter more as symbols of unity than for their power.
Early Heralds carried word between Chantries; phones have made this rare except when an item must be carried or a message proven genuine.
The Euthanatos made a staff that channelled Fate so the Council could mark its Heralds in a way even a novice could read.
